detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<CompilationError>) {\n502\t    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n503\t    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n504\t\n505\t    // Cargo compilation trace.write_test_metrics(&metrics) {\n902\t                tracing::warn!(\n903\t                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n904\t                    error = %e,\n905\t                    \"failed to write test metrics to trace file\"\n906\t                );\n907\t            }\n908\t\n909\t            // Write compilation errors if any were detected\n910\t            if !outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n911\t                if let Err(e) = trace.write_compilation_errors(&outcome.compilation_errors) {\n912\t                    tracing::warn!(\n913\t                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n914\t                        error = %e,\n915\t                        \"failed to write compilation errors to trace file\"\n916\t                    );\n917\t                }\n918\t            }\n919\t\n920\t            tracing::info!(\n921\t                bead_id = %bead_id,\n922\t                trace_dir = %trace.trace_dir().display(),\n923\t                stdout_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stdout.txt\").display(),\n924\t                stderr_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stderr.txt\").display(),\n925\t                metrics_path = exit_code = ?outcome.exit_code,\n928\t                duration_ms = outcome.duration.as_millis(),\n929\t                compilation_error_count = outcome.compilation_errors.len(),\n930\t                \"test output, metrics, and compilation errors written to bead trace files\"\n931\t            );\n932\t        } else {\n933\t            tracing::warn!(\n934\t                bead_id = %bead_id,\n935\t                \"failed to create bead trace directory, output files not written\"\n936\t            );\n937\t        }\n938\t\n939\t        Ok(outcome)\n940\t    }\n941\t}\n942\t\n943\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n944\t// Utility Functions\n945\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n946\t\n947\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n948\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n949\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n950\t        s.to_string()\n951\t    } else {\n952\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n953\t        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n954\t    }\n955\t}\n956\t\n957\t/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n958\t///\n959\t/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n960\t///\n961\t/// ## Example\n962\t///\n963\t/// ```\n964\t/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n965\t///\n966\t/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n967\t/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n968\t/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n969\t/// ```\n970\tpub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n971\t    let mut combined = String::new();\n972\t\n973\t    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n974\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n975\t        combined.push_str(stdout);\n976\t        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n977\t            combined.push('\\n');\n978\t        }\n979\t    }\n980\t\n981\t    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n982\t        if !combined.is_empty() {\n983\t            combined.push('\\n');\n984\t        }\n985\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n986\t        combined.push_str(stderr);\n987\t        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n988\t            combined.push('\\n');\n989\t        }\n990\t    }\n991\t\n992\t    combined\n993\t}\n994\t\n995\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n996\t// \"E0259\" | \"E0260\" | \"E0261\" | \"E0262\" | \"E0271\" | \"E0272\"\n            | \"E0273\" | \"E0274\" | \"E0275\" | \"E0276\" | \"E0278\" | \"E0279\" | \"E0280\" | \"E0281\"\n            | \"E0282\" | \"E0283\" | \"E0284\" => CompilationErrorVariant::TraitBound,\n\n            // Syntax errors (typically no error code, detected via pattern)\n            _ if code.is_empty() => CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax,\n\n            // Unused code warnings\n            _ if code == \"unused\" || code == \"dead_code\" || code == \"unused_variables\"\n                || code == \"unused_imports\" || code == \"unused_mut\" =>\n                CompilationErrorVariant::Unused,\n\n            // Default to unknown for unclassified error codes\n            _ => CompilationErrorVariant::Unknown,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a human-readable name for this variant.\n    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        match self {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::TypeMismatch => \"Type Mismatch\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::BorrowChecker => \"Borrow Checker\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::ImportOrPath => \"Import/Path\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Lifetime => \"Lifetime\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::TraitBound => \"Trait Bound\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax => \"Syntax\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Unused => \"Unused Code\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Other => \"Other\",\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Unknown => \"Unknown\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Detailed compilation error information.\n///\n/// Represents a single compilation error parsed from cargo test stderr.\n/// Includes the error code, message, file location, and classification.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct CompilationError {\n    /// Rust error code (e.g., \"E0308\").\n    pub code: Option<String>,\n    /// Error variant classification.\n    pub variant: CompilationErrorVariant,\n    /// Full error message.\n    pub message: String,\n    /// File path where the error occurred.\n    pub file: Option<String>,\n    /// Line number (1-indexed).\n    pub line: Option<usize>,\n    /// Column number (1-indexed).\n    pub column: Option<usize>,\n}\n\nimpl CompilationError {\n    /// Create a new compilation error.\n    pub fn new(\n        code: Option<String>,\n        message: String,\n        file: Option<String>,\n        line: Option<usize>,\n        column: Option<usize>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let variant = if let Some(ref code) = code {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::from_code(code)\n        } else {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax\n        };\n\n        CompilationError {\n            code,\n            variant,\n            message,\n            file,\n            line,\n            column,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a compilation error from an error line and optional location info.\n    pub fn from_error_line(line: &str) -> Self {\n        let (code, message) = Self::parse_error_code_and_message(line);\n        let variant = code\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|c| CompilationErrorVariant::from_code(c))\n            .unwrap_or(CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax);\n\n        CompilationError {\n            code,\n            variant,\n            message,\n            file: None,\n            line: None,\n            column: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse error code and message from an error line.\n    fn parse_error_code_and_message(line: &str) -> (Option<String>, String) {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Match \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\" pattern\n        if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n            if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n                let error_code = line[start + 6..end].to_string();\n                let message = if end + 1 < line.len() {\n                    let rest = line[end + 1..].trim();\n                    if rest.starts_with(':') {\n                        rest[1..].trim().to_string()\n                    } else {\n                        rest.to_string()\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    String::new()\n                };\n                return (Some(error_code), message);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No error code found\n        (None, line.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TestOutcome {\n    /// Returns true if cargo test exited with code 0.\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to compilation errors.\n    pub fn is_compilation_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to test failures (not compilation).\n    pub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.success() && !self.timed_out && !self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a human-readable summary of the outcome.\n    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {\n        if self.timed_out {\n            format!(\"Timed out after {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else if self.compilation_failed {\n            format!(\n                \"Compilation failed with {} error(s) in {:?}\",\n                self.compilation_errors.len(),\n                self.duration\n            )\n        } else if self.success() {\n            format!(\"Passed in {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else {\n            format!(\n                \"Failed with exit code {:?} in {:?}\",\n                self.exit_code, self.duration\n            )\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a summary of compilation errors, if any.\n    pub fn compilation_error_summary(&self) -> Option<String> {\n        if self.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        let mut summary = format!(\"{} compilation error(s):\\n\", self.compilation_errors.len());\n\n        for (i, error) in self.compilation_errors.iter().enumerate() {\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\"  {}. \", i + 1));\n\n            // Add error code if present\n            if let Some(ref code) = error.code {\n                summary.push_str(&format!(\"[{}] \", code));\n            }\n\n            // Add variant name\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\"({})\", error.variant.name()));\n\n            // Add message (truncated if too long)\n            let message = if error.message.len() > 80 {\n                format!(\"{}...\", &error.message[..77])\n            } else {\n                error.message.clone()\n            };\n            summary.push_str(&format!(\": {}\\n\", message));\n\n            // Add file location if available\n            if let Some(ref file) = error.file {\n                summary.push_str(&format!(\"     at {}:{}\", file,\n                    error.line.unwrap_or(0)));\n                if let Some(col) = error.column {\n                    summary.push_str(&format!(\":{}\", col));\n                }\n                summary.push('\\n');\n            }\n        }\n\n        Some(summary)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert this outcome to structured metrics.\n    pub fn to_metrics(&self, test_name: String) -> TestMetrics {\n        TestMetrics {\n            test_name,\n            exit_code: self.exit_code,\n            duration_ms: self.duration.as_millis() as u64,\n            timed_out: self.timed_out,\n            stdout_len: self.stdout.len(),\n            stderr_len: self.stderr.len(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Metrics\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Structured test metrics for storage and analysis.\n///\n/// This type captures the essential metrics from a test run in a\n/// serializable format that can be written to disk or sent to\n/// telemetry systems.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct TestMetrics {\n    /// Name of the test that was run.\n    pub test_name: String,\n    /// Exit code from cargo test (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test run in milliseconds.\n    pub duration_ms: u64,\n    /// Whether the test timed out.\n    pub timed_out: bool,\n    /// Length of captured stdout in bytes.\n    pub stdout_len: usize,\n    /// Length of captured stderr in bytes.\n    pub stderr_len: usize,\n    /// When the test completed.\n    pub timestamp: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,\n}\n\nimpl TestMetrics {\n    /// Returns true if the test succeeded (exit code 0 and no timeout).\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Get the duration as a Duration.\n    pub fn duration(&self) -> Duration {\n        Duration::from_millis(self.duration_ms)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Compilation Error Detection\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n///\n/// Returns (compilation_failed, errors) where compilation_failed is true\n/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and errors is a list\n/// of parsed compilation errors.\npub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<CompilationError>) {\n    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n    let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n\n    for line in stderr.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            let error = CompilationError::from_error_line(line);\n            errors.push(error);\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            // Preserve the original error message for test verification\n            let message = line.trim().to_string();\n            errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                let message = format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count);\n                errors.push(CompilationError::new(None, message, None, None, None));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                let error = CompilationError::new(\n                    Some(\"unused\".to_string()),\n                    line.to_string(),\n                    None,\n                    None,\n                    None,\n                );\n                errors.push(error);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, errors)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process with timeout handling\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n\n        // Use a thread to handle output() with timeout\n        let output_result = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            cmd.output()\n        });\n\n        // Wait for thread completion with timeout\n        let output = loop {\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                    exit_code: None,\n                    stdout: String::new(),\n                    stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                    duration: start.elapsed(),\n                    timed_out: true,\n                    compilation_failed: false,\n                    compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            // Check if thread is complete\n            if output_result.is_finished() {\n                match output_result.join() {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => break output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to execute cargo test: {}\", e))\n                            .with_context(|| \"failed to spawn or execute cargo test\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cargo test thread panicked\"));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n        };\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to bead trace directory.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout and stderr\n    /// to files in the `.beads/traces/<bead-id>/` directory. This is used to\n    /// record test execution output for debugging and analysis.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `bead_id` - The bead ID to use for the trace directory name\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Trace directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let bead_id = \"bf-12345\";\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(bead_id).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_bead_trace(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create bead trace directory and write outputs\n        let bead_id = BeadId::from(bead_id);\n        if let Some(trace) = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write test metrics (exit code, duration, etc.)\n            let test_name = format!(\"cargo_test_{}\", bead_id.as_ref());\n            let metrics = outcome.to_metrics(test_name);\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_test_metrics(&metrics) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write test metrics to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write compilation errors if any were detected\n            if !outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n                if let Err(e) = trace.write_compilation_errors(&outcome.compilation_errors) {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to write compilation errors to trace file\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                trace_dir = %trace.trace_dir().display(),\n                stdout_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stdout.txt\").display(),\n                stderr_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stderr.txt\").display(),\n                metrics_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"test_metrics.json\").display(),\n                compilation_errors_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"compilation_errors.json\").display(),\n                exit_code = ?outcome.exit_code,\n                duration_ms = outcome.duration.as_millis(),\n                compilation_error_count = outcome.compilation_errors.len(),\n                \"test output, metrics, and compilation errors written to bead trace files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                \"failed to create bead trace directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::fs;\n    use tempfile::TempDir;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_args_default_is_empty() {\n        let args = TestArgs::new();\n        assert!(args.target.is_none());\n        assert!(args.filter.is_none());\n        assert!(args.test_names.is_empty());\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n308\t// Trace retention cleanup\n309\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n310\t\n311\t/// Cleanup result for trace retention.\n312\t#[derive(Debug, Default)]\n313\tpub struct TraceCleanupSummary {\n314\t    /// Number of traces pruned (metadata kept).\n315\t    pub traces_pruned: u32,\n316\t    /// Number of traces fully deleted.\n317\t    pub traces_deleted: u32,\n318\t}\n319\t\n320\t/// Clean up old traces based on retention policy.\n321\t///\n322\t/// - Failed beads (non-zero exit): delete after 30 days\n323\t/// - Successful beads (exit 0): prune data after 7 days, keep metadata only\n324\tpub fn cleanup_traces(\n325\t    traces_dir: &Path,\n326\t    retention_days_failed: u32,\n327\t    retention_days_success: u32,\n328\t) -> Result<TraceCleanupSummary> {\n329\t    let mut summary = TraceCleanupSummary::default();\n330\t\n331\t    if !traces_dir.exists() {\n332\t        return Ok(summary);\n333\t    }\n334\t\n335\t    let now = SystemTime::now()\n336\t        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n337\t        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n338\t        .unwrap_or(0);\n339\t\n340\t    // Iterate through bead trace directories.\n341\t    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(traces_dir)\n342\t        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read traces directory: {}\", traces_dir.display()))?\n343\t    {\n344\t        let entry = match entry {\n345\t            Ok(e) => e,\n346\t            Err(_) => continue,\n347\t        };\n348\t\n349\t        let path = entry.path();\n350\t\n351\t        // Only process directories (bead-id subdirectories).\n352\t        if !path.is_dir() {\n353\t            continue;\n354\t        }\n355\t\n356\t        // Check metadata.json to determine outcome and age.\n357\t        let metadata_path = path.join(\"metadata.json\");\n358\t        let metadata: Option<TraceMetadata> = metadata_path\n359\t            .exists()\n360\t            .then(|| {\n361\t                let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path).ok()?;\n362\t                serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()\n363\t            })\n364\t            .flatten();\n365\t\n366\t        let age_days = metadata\n367\t            .as_ref()\n368\t            .and_then(|m| now.checked_sub(m.captured_at.timestamp() as u64))\n369\t            .map(|secs| secs / 86400)\n370\t            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n371\t\n372\t        let is_failed = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.exit_code != 0).unwrap_or(false);\n373\t        let is_pruned = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.pruned).unwrap_or(false);\n374\t\n375\t        // Check if trace data files actually exist before attempting to prune.\n376\t        // This prevents counting a trace as \"pruned\" when the data files were\n377\t        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n378\t        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n379\t        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n380\t        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"]\n381\t            .iter()\n382\t            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n383\t\n384\t        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n385\t        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n386\t        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n387\t        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n388\t        let should_prune =\n389\t            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n390\t\n391\t        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n392\t        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n393\t        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n394\t            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n395\t                tracing::debug!(\n396\t                    path = %path.display(),\n397\t                    error = %e,\n398\t                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n399\t                );\n400\t            }\n401\t        }\n402\t\n403\t        if should_delete {\n404\t            // Delete entire trace directory.\n405\t            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n406\t                tracing::warn!(\n407\t                    path = %path.display(),\n408\t                    error = %e,\n409\t                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n410\t                );\n411\t            } else {\n412\t                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n413\t            }\n414\t        } else if should_prune {\n415\t            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n416\t            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n417\t                tracing::warn!(\n418\t                    path = %path.display(),\n419\t                    error = %e,\n420\t                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n421\t                );\n422\t            } else {\n423\t                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n424\t            }\n425\t        }\n426\t    }\n427\t\n428\t    Ok(summary)\n429\t}\n430\t\n431\t/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n432\t/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\n433\tfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n434\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n435\t    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n436\t        return Ok(());\n437\t    }\n438\t\n439\t    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n440\t    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n441\t        if !metadata.pruned {\n442\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n443\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n444\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n445\t            tracing::debug!(\n446\t                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n447\t                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n448\t            );\n449\t        }\n450\t    }\n451\t    Ok(())\n452\t}\n453\t\n454\t/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n455\t///\n456\t/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n457\t/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n458\t/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n459\t/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n460\t/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\n461\tfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n462\t    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n463\t    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n464\t    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n465\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n466\t    if metadata_path.exists() {\n467\t        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n468\t        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n469\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n470\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n471\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n472\t        }\n473\t    }\n474\t\n475\t    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n476\t    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n477\t    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n478\t    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"] {\n479\t        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n480\t        if path.exists() {\n481\t            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n482\t                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n483\t        }\n484\t    }\n485\t\n486\t    Ok(())\n487\t}\n488\t\n489\tuse std::time::SystemTime;\n490\t\n491\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n492\t// Tests\n493\t// `.beads/`.\n    /// Returns `None` if trace capture is disabled.\n    pub fn new(bead_id: &BeadId, beads_root: &Path) -> Option<Self> {\n        Self::new_with_sanitizer(bead_id, beads_root, None)\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new trace capture for a bead with an optional sanitizer.\n    ///\n    /// When `sanitizer` is `Some`, all trace content is sanitized synchronously\n    /// before writing to disk (no unsanitized window on disk).\n    pub fn new_with_sanitizer(\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        beads_root: &Path,\n        sanitizer: Option<Arc<Sanitizer>>,\n    ) -> Option<Self> {\n        let trace_dir = beads_root\n            .join(\".beads\")\n            .join(\"traces\")\n            .join(bead_id.as_ref());\n\n        // Create the trace directory.\n        if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&trace_dir) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to create trace directory, trace capture disabled\"\n            );\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        Some(TraceCapture {\n            trace_dir,\n            enabled: true,\n            sanitizer,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the trace directory path.\n    pub fn trace_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.trace_dir\n    }\n\n    /// Write stdout to `stdout.txt`.\n    ///\n    /// Content is sanitized before writing if a sanitizer is configured.\n    pub fn write_stdout(&self, stdout: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let content = self.sanitize(stdout);\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"stdout.txt\");\n        std::fs::write(&path, content.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write stdout trace: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Write stderr to `stderr.txt`.\n    ///\n    /// Content is sanitized before writing if a sanitizer is configured.\n    pub fn write_stderr(&self, stderr: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let content = self.sanitize(stderr);\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"stderr.txt\");\n        std::fs::write(&path, content.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write stderr trace: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Write structured trace JSONL to `trace.jsonl`.\n    ///\n    /// Each line should be a valid JSON object. Lines are sanitized before\n    /// writing if a sanitizer is configured.\n    pub fn write_trace_jsonl(&self, trace_lines: &[String]) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled || trace_lines.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"trace.jsonl\");\n        let joined = trace_lines.join(\"\\n\");\n        let content = self.sanitize(&joined);\n        std::fs::write(&path, content.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write trace JSONL: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Sanitize text if a sanitizer is configured; otherwise return as-is.\n    fn sanitize<'a>(&self, text: &'a str) -> std::borrow::Cow<'a, str> {\n        match &self.sanitizer {\n            Some(s) => std::borrow::Cow::Owned(s.sanitize(text)),\n            None => std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(text),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Write metadata to `metadata.json`.\n    pub fn write_metadata(&self, metadata: &TraceMetadata) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n        let json =\n            serde_json::to_string_pretty(metadata).context(\"failed to serialize trace metadata\")?;\n        std::fs::write(&path, json)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write metadata: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Write test metrics to `test_metrics.json`.\n    ///\n    /// This stores cargo test execution metrics including exit code,\n    /// duration, and output sizes for later analysis.\n    pub fn write_test_metrics(&self, metrics: &TestMetrics) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"test_metrics.json\");\n        let json =\n            serde_json::to_string_pretty(metrics).context(\"failed to serialize test metrics\")?;\n        std::fs::write(&path, json)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write test metrics: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Write compilation errors to `compilation_errors.json`.\n    ///\n    /// This stores detailed compilation error information including error codes,\n    /// variant classifications, and file locations for later analysis.\n    pub fn write_compilation_errors(&self, errors: &[crate::cargo_test::CompilationError]) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled || errors.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(\"compilation_errors.json\");\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(errors)\n            .context(\"failed to serialize compilation errors\")?;\n        std::fs::write(&path, json)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write compilation errors: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Finalize the trace and return the trace directory path.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if trace capture was disabled.\n    pub fn finalize(self) -> Option<PathBuf> {\n        if self.enabled {\n            Some(self.trace_dir)\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Delete the entire trace directory.\n    pub fn delete(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.trace_dir.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.trace_dir).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to delete trace directory: {}\",\n                    self.trace_dir.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Prune trace data (keep metadata only).\n    ///\n    /// Deletes trace.jsonl, stdout.txt, and stderr.txt, keeping only metadata.json.\n    /// Updates the `pruned` flag in metadata.\n    pub fn prune_trace_data(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Delete trace data files.\n        for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"] {\n            let path = self.trace_dir.join(file);\n            if path.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Update metadata to mark as pruned.\n        let metadata_path = self.trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n        if metadata_path.exists() {\n            let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n            if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n                metadata.pruned = true;\n                let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n                std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Trace format detection\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Detect trace format from agent adapter name.\npub fn detect_trace_format(agent_name: &str) -> TraceFormat {\n    match agent_name {\n        n if n.starts_with(\"claude-\") => TraceFormat::ClaudeJson,\n        n if n.contains(\"codex\") || n.contains(\"openai\") => TraceFormat::OpenaiJsonl,\n        n if n.contains(\"aider\") => TraceFormat::AiderMarkdown,\n        _ => TraceFormat::RawText,\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Trace retention cleanup\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Cleanup result for trace retention.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct TraceCleanupSummary {\n    /// Number of traces pruned (metadata kept).\n    pub traces_pruned: u32,\n    /// Number of traces fully deleted.\n    pub traces_deleted: u32,\n}\n\n/// Clean up old traces based on retention policy.\n///\n/// - Failed beads (non-zero exit): delete after 30 days\n/// - Successful beads (exit 0): prune data after 7 days, keep metadata only\npub fn cleanup_traces(\n    traces_dir: &Path,\n    retention_days_failed: u32,\n    retention_days_success: u32,\n) -> Result<TraceCleanupSummary> {\n    let mut summary = TraceCleanupSummary::default();\n\n    if !traces_dir.exists() {\n        return Ok(summary);\n    }\n\n    let now = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    // Iterate through bead trace directories.\n    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(traces_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read traces directory: {}\", traces_dir.display()))?\n    {\n        let entry = match entry {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n\n        let path = entry.path();\n\n        // Only process directories (bead-id subdirectories).\n        if !path.is_dir() {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check metadata.json to determine outcome and age.\n        let metadata_path = path.join(\"metadata.json\");\n        let metadata: Option<TraceMetadata> = metadata_path\n            .exists()\n            .then(|| {\n                let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path).ok()?;\n                serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()\n            })\n            .flatten();\n\n        let age_days = metadata\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|m| now.checked_sub(m.captured_at.timestamp() as u64))\n            .map(|secs| secs / 86400)\n            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n\n        let is_failed = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.exit_code != 0).unwrap_or(false);\n        let is_pruned = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.pruned).unwrap_or(false);\n\n        // Check if trace data files actually exist before attempting to prune.\n        // This prevents counting a trace as \"pruned\" when the data files were\n        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"]\n            .iter()\n            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n\n        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n        let should_prune =\n            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n\n        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        if should_delete {\n            // Delete entire trace directory.\n            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n            }\n        } else if should_prune {\n            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(summary)\n}\n\n/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\nfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n        if !metadata.pruned {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n///\n/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\nfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if metadata_path.exists() {\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"] {\n        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n        if path.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nuse std::time::SystemTime;\n\n// This enables post-mortem analysis of failed test runs and distinguishes between compilation failures and runtime test failures.\n8\t\n9\t## Architecture\n10\t\n11\t### Components\n12\t\n13\t1. **CompilationError** - Detailed error structure with code, variant, message, and location\n14\t2. **CompilationErrorVariant** - Enum classifying errors by type (TypeMismatch, BorrowChecker, etc.)\n15\t3. **detect_compilation_errors()** - Parses stderr to extract errors\n16\t4. **TraceCapture::write_compilation_errors()** - Writes errors to trace directory\n17\t5. **CargoTest::run_with_bead_trace()** - Orchestrates the full workflow\n18\t\n19\t### Data Flow\n20\t\n21\t```\n22\tcargo test execution\n23\t    ↓\n24\tstdout/stderr capture\n25\t    ↓\n26\tdetect_compilation_errors(stderr)\n27\t    ↓\n28\tTestOutcome { compilation_failed, compilation_errors }\n29\t    ↓\n30\trun_with_bead_trace()\n31\t    ↓\n32\tTraceCapture writes:\n33\t    - stdout.txt\n34\t    - stderr.txt\n35\t    - test_metrics.json\n36\t    - compilation_errors.json (if errors detected)\n37\t```\n38\t\n39\t## Error Classification\n40\t\n41\t### Supported Error Variants\n42\t\n43\t| Variant | Description | Example Error Codes |\n44\t|--------|-------------|---------------------|\n45\t| TypeMismatch | Type incompatibility errors | E0308, E0309, E0061, E0063 |\n46\t| BorrowChecker | Ownership/lifetime violations | E0382, E0502, E0505, E0506 |\n47\t| ImportOrPath | Module/import resolution failures | E0432, E0433, E0583, E0603 |\n48\t| Lifetime | Lifetime annotation errors | E0495, E0597, E0623 |\n49\t| TraitBound | Trait constraint violations | E0277, E0207, E0119 |\n50\t| Syntax | Parse/syntax errors | (no error code) |\n51\t| Unused | Dead code warnings treated as errors | unused_variables, dead_code |\n52\t| Other | Unclassified compiler errors | - |\n53\t| Unknown | Error codes not in classification | - |\n54\t\n55\t## Full Test Execution Flow\n56\t\n57\t### 1. Test Execution Initiation\n58\t\n59\t```rust\n60\tlet runner = CargoTest::new(workspace_path);\n61\tlet bead_id = \"bf-12345\";\n62\t\n63\t// Execute with trace capture\n64\tlet outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(bead_id)?;\n65\t```\n66\t\n67\t### 2. Process Spawning and Output Capture\n68\t\n69\tThe system spawns a cargo test process with:\n70\t- Configured timeout (default: 600 seconds)\n71\t- Piped stdout and stderr for capture\n72\t- Thread-based monitoring for timeout enforcement\n73\t\n74\t```rust\n75\tlet mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n76\tcmd.args(&args);\n77\tcmd.current_dir(&workspace);\n78\tcmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n79\tcmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n80\t```\n81\t\n82\t### 3. Output Parsing and Error Detection\n83\t\n84\tAfter process completion, the system parses stderr:\n85\t\n86\t```rust\n87\tlet (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n88\t    detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\tThe `detect_compilation_errors()` function identifies:\n92\t- `error[E####]:` patterns - Rust compiler errors with codes\n93\t- `could not compile` messages - Compilation failure indicators\n94\t- `aborting due to N previous errors` - Error count summaries\n95\t- `error:` with unused/dead_code - Warnings treated as errors\n96\t\n97\t### 4. Output File Writing\n126\t\n127\tFor each output type, the system:\n128\t\n129\t```rust\n130\t// Write stdout\n131\ttrace.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout)?;\n132\t\n133\t// Write stderr\n134\ttrace.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr)?;\n135\t\n136\t// Write test metrics\n137\tlet metrics = outcome.to_metrics(test_name);\n138\ttrace.write_test_metrics(&metrics)?;\n139\t\n140\t// Write compilation errors (if present)\n141\tif !outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n142\t    trace.write_compilation_errors(&outcome.compilation_errors)?;\n143\t}\n144\t```\n145\t\n146\t### 7. self.compilation_failed\n191\t}\n192\t\n193\tpub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n194\t    !self.success() && !self.timed_out && !self.compilation_failed\n195\t}\n196\t\n197\tpub fn success(&self) This enables post-mortem analysis of failed test runs and distinguishes between compilation failures and runtime test failures.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Components\n\n1. **CompilationError** - Detailed error structure with code, variant, message, and location\n2. **CompilationErrorVariant** - Enum classifying errors by type (TypeMismatch, BorrowChecker, etc.)\n3. **detect_compilation_errors()** - Parses stderr to extract errors\n4. **TraceCapture::write_compilation_errors()** - Writes errors to trace directory\n5. **CargoTest::run_with_bead_trace()** - Orchestrates the full workflow\n\n### Data Flow\n\n```\ncargo test execution\n    ↓\nstdout/stderr capture\n    ↓\ndetect_compilation_errors(stderr)\n    ↓\nTestOutcome { compilation_failed, compilation_errors }\n    ↓\nrun_with_bead_trace()\n    ↓\nTraceCapture writes:\n    - stdout.txt\n    - stderr.txt\n    - test_metrics.json\n    - compilation_errors.json (if errors detected)\n```\n\n## Error Classification\n\n### Supported Error Variants\n\n| Variant | Description | Example Error Codes |\n|--------|-------------|---------------------|\n| TypeMismatch | Type incompatibility errors | E0308, E0309, E0061, E0063 |\n| BorrowChecker | Ownership/lifetime violations | E0382, E0502, E0505, E0506 |\n| ImportOrPath | Module/import resolution failures | E0432, E0433, E0583, E0603 |\n| Lifetime | Lifetime annotation errors | E0495, E0597, E0623 |\n| TraitBound | Trait constraint violations | E0277, E0207, E0119 |\n| Syntax | Parse/syntax errors | (no error code) |\n| Unused | Dead code warnings treated as errors | unused_variables, dead_code |\n| Other | Unclassified compiler errors | - |\n| Unknown | Error codes not in classification | - |\n\n## Full Test Execution Flow\n\n### 1. Test Execution Initiation\n\n```rust\nlet runner = CargoTest::new(workspace_path);\nlet bead_id = \"bf-12345\";\n\n// Execute with trace capture\nlet outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(bead_id)?;\n```\n\n### 2. Process Spawning and Output Capture\n\nThe system spawns a cargo test process with:\n- Configured timeout (default: 600 seconds)\n- Piped stdout and stderr for capture\n- Thread-based monitoring for timeout enforcement\n\n```rust\nlet mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\ncmd.args(&args);\ncmd.current_dir(&workspace);\ncmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\ncmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n```\n\n### 3. Output Parsing and Error Detection\n\nAfter process completion, the system parses stderr:\n\n```rust\nlet (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n    detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n```\n\nThe `detect_compilation_errors()` function identifies:\n- `error[E####]:` patterns - Rust compiler errors with codes\n- `could not compile` messages - Compilation failure indicators\n- `aborting due to N previous errors` - Error count summaries\n- `error:` with unused/dead_code - Warnings treated as errors\n\n### 4. Outcome Construction\n\nThe `TestOutcome` struct captures:\n\n```rust\npub struct TestOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n    pub duration: Duration,\n    pub timed_out: bool,\n    pub compilation_failed: bool,\n    pub compilation_errors: Vec<CompilationError>,\n}\n```\n\n### 5. Trace Directory Creation\n\nThe system creates the trace directory structure:\n\n```\n.beads/traces/<bead-id>/\n├── stdout.txt\n├── stderr.txt\n├── test_metrics.json\n└── compilation_errors.json (if errors present)\n```\n\n### 6. Output File Writing\n\nFor each output type, the system:\n\n```rust\n// Write stdout\ntrace.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout)?;\n\n// Write stderr\ntrace.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr)?;\n\n// Write test metrics\nlet metrics = outcome.to_metrics(test_name);\ntrace.write_test_metrics(&metrics)?;\n\n// Write compilation errors (if present)\nif !outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty() {\n    trace.write_compilation_errors(&outcome.compilation_errors)?;\n}\n```\n\n### 7. Error Classification and Serialization\n\nEach compilation error is classified:\n\n```rust\nimpl CompilationError {\n    pub fn new(\n        code: Option<String>,\n        message: String,\n        file: Option<String>,\n        line: Option<usize>,\n        column: Option<usize>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let variant = if let Some(ref code) = code {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::from_code(code)\n        } else {\n            CompilationErrorVariant::Syntax\n        };\n        // ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\nThe error is then serialized to JSON:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"code\": \"E0308\",\n    \"variant\": \"TypeMismatch\",\n    \"message\": \"mismatched types\",\n    \"file\": \"src/main.rs\",\n    \"line\": 10,\n    \"column\": 5\n  }\n]\n```\n\n### 8. Outcome Determination\n\nThe system classifies the overall outcome:\n\n```rust\npub fn is_compilation_failure(&self) -> bool {\n    self.compilation_failed\n}\n\npub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n    !self.success() && !self.timed_out && !self.compilation_failed\n}\n\npub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n    self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n}\n```\n\n## Trace Output Structure\n\n### stdout.txt\n\nRaw stdout from cargo test execution, including:\n- Compilation progress messages\n- Test execution output\n- Test results\n\n### stderr.txt\n\nRaw stderr from cargo test execution, including:\n- Compiler error messages\n- Warning messages\n- Test failure output\n\n### test_metrics.json\n\nStructured test execution metrics:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"test_name\": \"cargo_test_bf-12345\",\n  \"exit_code\": 101,\n  \"duration_ms\": 1234,\n  \"timed_out\": false,\n  \"stdout_len\": 1024,\n  \"stderr_len\": 2048,\n  \"timestamp\": \"2026-07-14T12:34:56.789Z\"\n}\n```\n\n### compilation_errors.json\n\nDetailed compilation error information (only present when compilation fails):\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"code\": \"E0308\",\n    \"variant\": \"TypeMismatch\",\n    \"message\": \"mismatched types: expected `i32`, found `&str`\",\n    \"file\": \"src/main.rs\",\n    \"line\": 10,\n    \"column\": 5\n  },\n  {\n    \"code\": \"E0382\",\n    \"variant\": \"BorrowChecker\",\n    \"message\": \"use of moved value\",\n    \"file\": \"src/main.rs\",\n    \"line\": 15,\n    \"column\": 8\n  }\n]\n```\n\n## Example Workflow\n\n### Successful Compilation\n\n```rust\n// Test code compiles and passes\nlet runner = CargoTest::new(workspace);\nlet outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(\"bf-success\")?;\n\nassert!(outcome.success());\nassert!(!outcome.is_compilation_failure());\nassert!(outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty());\n\n// Trace directory contains:\n// - stdout.txt (test output)\n// - stderr.txt (warnings, if any)\n// - test_metrics.json (exit_code: 0)\n// compilation_errors.json (NOT created)\n```\n\n### Compilation Failure\n\n```rust\n// Test code has type mismatch\nlet runner = CargoTest::new(workspace);\nlet outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(\"bf-compile-fail\")?;\n\nassert!(!outcome.success());\nassert!(outcome.is_compilation_failure());\nassert!(!outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty());\n\n// Verify specific error\nlet type_errors: Vec<_> = outcome.compilation_errors\n    .iter()\n    .filter(|e| e.code.as_deref() == Some(\"E0308\"))\n    .collect();\nassert!(!type_errors.is_empty());\n\n// Trace directory contains:\n// - stdout.txt (compilation progress)\n// - stderr.txt (compiler errors)\n// - test_metrics.json (exit_code: 101)\n// - compilation_errors.json (E0308 error details)\n```\n\n### Test Failure (No Compilation Errors)\n\n```rust\n// Test code compiles but test fails\nlet runner = CargoTest::new(workspace);\nlet outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(\"bf-test-fail\")?;\n\nassert!(!outcome.success());\nassert!(!outcome.is_compilation_failure());\nassert!(outcome.is_test_failure());\nassert!(outcome.compilation_errors.is_empty());\n\n// Trace directory contains:\n// - stdout.txt (test execution output)\n// - stderr.txt (test failure messages)\n// - test_metrics.json (exit_code: 1)\n// compilation_errors.json (NOT created)\n```\n\n## Error Detection Patterns\n\n### Type Mismatch (E0308)\n\n```\nerror[E0308]: mismatched types\n  --> src/main.rs:10:5\n   |\n10 |     let x: i32 = \"hello\";\n   |            ---   ^^^^^^^ expected `i32`, found `&str`\n```\n\nDetected as:\n- code: \"E0308\"\n- variant: TypeMismatch\n- file: \"src/main.rs\"\n- line: 10\n- column: 5\n\n### Borrow Checker (E0382)\n\n```\nerror[E0382]: use of moved value\n  --> src/main.rs:15:8\n   |\n15 |     let _used = s;\n   |                 ^ value moved here in previous iteration\n```\n\nDetected as:\n- code: \"E0382\"\n- variant: BorrowChecker\n- file: \"src/main.rs\"\n- line: 15\n- column: 8\n\n### Import Error (E0433)\n\n```\nerror[E0433]: failed to resolve: use of undeclared crate or module\n  --> src/main.rs:5:5\n   |\n5 | use nonexistent::Module;\n   |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ use of undeclared crate or module\n```\n\nDetected as:\n- code: \"E0433\"\n- variant: ImportOrPath\n- file: \"src/main.rs\"\n- line: 5\n- column: 5\n\n## Integration Tests\n\nThe system includes comprehensive end-to-end tests:\n\n### Test Coverage\n\n1. **test_end_to_end_compilation_error_workflow**\n   - Verifies compilation_errors.json is not created for test failures\n\n### Running Tests\n\n```bash\n# Run all compilation error detection tests\ncargo test --test compilation_error_detection\n\n# Run specific end-to-end test\ncargo test test_end_to_end_compilation_error_workflow\n\n# Run with output\ncargo test --test compilation_error_detection -- --nocapture\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### No compilation_errors.json Created\n\nIf compilation errors occurred but no JSON file was created:\n1.
